sentences.text: Using high-resolution imaging to observe pioneer axons in the inner ear, researchers found that the chemical signal Cxcl14 directs these axons to grow, turn, and bundle correctly.

When Cxcl14 was removed, axons failed to navigate properly, hair cell connections were damaged, and hearing-related behaviors were impaired, demonstrating that pioneer axons are necessary for the growth and movement of other neurons.
The authors conclude that their results define a new way that chemical signals help build the early sensory circuits needed for hearing.
